summary: Dual-output color conversion structurally twin to TexturePaletteColorLookup (0x0051CE2A) but writing two independent destination rows. Reads three source streams from the a2 array (a0 pair at byte offset 8*a3, a1/a2 at 4*a3), indexes four lookup tables by bytes from those streams, and writes 3 output bytes per pixel into each of two destination streams held at *a4 and *(a4+4). The main loop converts two pixels per stream per iteration and runs a1[23] >> 1 times; an odd row width writes one trailing pixel per stream. Each output channel is byte(source byte + table value + base), middle channel blending two tables via >> 16.

operations.description: Load the LUT sub-object v4 from this->+0x19C (a1[103]); its entries v4[4..7] hold the four lookup tables.
Read the additive base from this->+0x11C (a1[71]) and the row width from this->+0x5C (a1[23]).
Read the four lookup-table pointers from v4[4] (+0x1AC), v4[5] (+0x1B0), v4[6] (+0x1B4) and v4[7] (+0x1B8).
Resolve source streams: the a2[0] entry yields a pointer pair at byte offset 8*a3, and a2[1]/a2[2] yield pointers at 4*a3; take two destination rows from *a4 and *(a4+4).
When a1[23] >> 1 is zero the two-pixel-per-stream loop is skipped entirely.
Two-pixel-per-stream loop running a1[23] >> 1 times, writing 12 output bytes per iteration (6 into each destination stream).
Index the four tables by bytes from the two auxiliary source streams; the middle channel sums two table values and shifts the sum >> 16.
Write two RGB pixels per destination stream per iteration, each channel computed as byte(source byte + table value + base).
When the row width is odd (a1[23] & 1), process one trailing pixel in each destination stream after the loop.
Write the final 3-byte pixel into each of the two destination streams using the same table lookups and base addition.
Return the low byte of the last computed channel value (LOBYTE of the base register v5).
